hints: Focus on whether a new insoluble solid is actually formed, not just whether a solid is present at the start.
Recall that Group 2 hydroxides get more soluble down the group, but calcium hydroxide is still sparingly soluble and forms a white suspension, while barium sulfate is famously insoluble.
Check each test-tube for a precipitation or for a solid that dissolves away, then count only those that finish with a white solid product.
walkthrough:
**Recall what counts as a white solid product**

A white solid product means a precipitate or insoluble solid is made in the reaction. A solid reactant that simply dissolves away does not count.

Rule to use: precipitate forms if product is insoluble in water.

**Test-tube 1: Calcium + water**

Calcium is reactive and gives calcium hydroxide plus hydrogen.

$$\text{Ca(s) + 2H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{Ca(OH)}_2\text{(s/aq) + H}_2\text{(g)}$$ 
$\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ is sparingly soluble, so it appears as a white solid suspension. This is one white solid product.

**Test-tube 2: Barium chloride + strontium hydroxide**

This would swap to give barium hydroxide and strontium chloride.

$$\text{BaCl}_2\text{(aq) + Sr(OH)}_2\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{Ba(OH)}_2\text{(aq) + SrCl}_2\text{(aq)}$$ 
All Group 2 chlorides are soluble and barium and strontium hydroxides are soluble enough to stay in solution, so no precipitate forms.

**Test-tube 3: Calcium carbonate + excess acid**

Carbonate plus acid gives a soluble salt, carbon dioxide and water.

$$\text{CaCO}_3\text{(s) + 2HCl(aq)} \rightarrow \text{CaCl}_2\text{(aq) + CO}_2\text{(g) + H}_2\text{O(l)}$$ 
The starting white solid $\text{CaCO}_3$ dissolves to give soluble $\text{CaCl}_2$. No solid product remains.

**Test-tube 4: Magnesium sulfate + barium nitrate**

This is a classic precipitation test for sulfate.

$$\text{MgSO}_4\text{(aq) + Ba(NO}_3\text{)}_2\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4\text{(s) + Mg(NO}_3\text{)}_2\text{(aq)}$$ 
$\text{BaSO}_4$ is insoluble and forms a dense white precipitate. This is the second white solid product.

**Count them up**

Only mixtures 1 and 4 finish with a white solid. That is 2 mixtures in total.

options.A: 0 is too low because you have missed the two precipitates. Calcium hydroxide from Ca + water and barium sulfate from MgSO4 + Ba(NO3)2 are both white solids.
options.B: 1 is too low. Many students spot the famous BaSO4 white precipitate but forget that Ca(OH)2 is sparingly soluble and also gives a white suspension.
options.C: 2 is correct. Mixture 1 gives sparingly soluble white Ca(OH)2 and mixture 4 gives insoluble white BaSO4. Mixtures 2 and 3 give only soluble aqueous products.
options.D: 3 is too high. Mixture 2 has no precipitate because Ba(OH)2 and SrCl2 are soluble, and mixture 3 has no solid product because CaCO3 dissolves to form soluble CaCl2.
